key_insight: SCP-FTLE and SCP-FSLE accelerate 3D Lagrangian flow diagnostics by combining CPU/GPU parallelism with memory- and data-movement-aware algorithms for FTLE and FSLE.
engineering_relevance: The workflow enables scalable, high-throughput detection of transport barriers and stretching structures in large CFD datasets, making advanced Lagrangian analysis practical for billion-seed and large-ensemble studies.
method: CPU- and GPU-accelerated FTLE/FSLE modules in StreamCenter+
Supports structured and native unstructured meshes with selectable integration/interpolation schemes
Uses rolling snapshot reuse, memory-bounded FTLE batching, device-resident trajectory state, and active-set FSLE advancement
evidence_signal: The paper reports state-of-the-art performance, with strong-scaling efficiency up to 86.3% on 32 GPUs for FTLE and 95.2% for FSLE, and verifies results on ABC, SCVM, linear stretching, and rotational shear benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful memory management, batching, and device-resident execution, so results may vary with mesh type, hardware, and chosen integration/interpolation settings.
paper_title: SCP-FTLE and SCP-FSLE: High-performance finite-time and finite-size Lyapunov-exponent computations for CPUs and GPUs
